Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmail Baghaei said on X that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio was distorting history to provide a philosophical and historical justification for U.S. warmongering. At the Acropolis, Marco Rubio (mis)presents the history of the West - from ancient Greece to the contemporary United States - as a single, seamless continuum. This is the logic of anachronism: a distortion of historical time produced by the careless fusion of categories such as Greece, Rome, Christianity, Europe, America, and, ultimately, “America First.” It is as if America has finally discovered that 'intimidation' can be staged more effectively beneath the neon lights of a philosophy of history than in the bare idiom of the cowboy. Rubio lifts the Greek concept of 'thumos' out of its historical and philosophical setting and recasts it as a celebration of power - of force exercised without law or justice - along with competition and national will. That reading misses a constitutive half of the Greek inheritance. Greece was not only a theater of power and glory. It was also the birthplace of the tragedy of hubris and aggression, from the myth of Troy and Homer’s Iliad; of the critique of imperial ambition in Thucydides’ History of the Peloponnesian War; of political philosophy in Plato’s Republic and Aristotle’s Politics; and of enduring meditations on the limits of power, moral responsibility, and human fate in Sophocles’ Antigone and Oedipus Rex. This other half of the Greek legacy is deliberately omitted from Rubio’s narrative. History is thereby converted from a field of inquiry and critical reflection into an instrument of political legitimation. What emerges is not a philosophy of history, but a manufactured narrative designed to authorize U.S. militancy and to construct a convenient political myth: a distorted reconstruction of the past in which the politics of the present are made to appear inevitable and historically ordained. Once history is pressed into the service of legitimizing power—the unlawful and unjust use of force—its purpose is no longer to understand the past, but to glorify power itself. Vasily Vereshchagin’s The Apotheosis of War offers a stark counter-image. Its pyramid of skulls, left behind by conquerors, confronts the mythology of glory with the material residue of conquest. It recalls what remains when history is reduced to the exaltation of power. At such a juncture, Western thinkers have a responsibility to defend history itself - and the philosophical complexity of Western civilization - against a distorted and apologetic reinterpretation by an aggressive power prepared to sacrifice a civilization’s human achievements in order to legitimize the unrestrained exercise of force. The danger lies not merely in misreading the past, but in appropriating it to authorize that force, and to aggrandize it, in the present.

As part of the ongoing consultations between the Islamic Consultative Assembly and the diplomatic apparatus on various foreign policy issues, a meeting was held on Tuesday evening with the participation of Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and a number of members of the Islamic Consultative Assembly. During the three-hour meeting, attended by Ali Babaei Karnamei, Chairman of the Social Affairs Commission, and a number of respected members of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, the Foreign Minister presented a comprehensive report on the discussions and activities undertaken during the delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran’s visit to New York to attend the 81st annual session of the United Nations General Assembly. Referring to his and the President’s numerous consultations with various countries participating in the UN General Assembly, the Foreign Minister stressed that the delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran, backed by the heroic resistance and steadfastness of the Iranian people in the face of the military aggression of its enemies, articulated Iran’s positions in the clearest and most authoritative manner possible. The Foreign Minister also referred to the use of the opportunity provided by the UN General Assembly session to explain Iran’s innovative approach and present a seven-day plan for restoring security to the Strait of Hormuz. He stressed that, based on instructions issued by the competent authorities of the country, the delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran presented Iran’s conditions and considerations to the mediators in the form of a precise and operational plan. It became clear to all that, just as the Islamic Republic of Iran is resolute and determined in defending itself, it is also serious about using the tools of diplomacy to safeguard its national interests and security. During the meeting, the Foreign Minister also responded to questions and discussed the proposals and views of the members of Parliament, providing explanations on a wide range of foreign policy and national security issues, including economic diplomacy, neutralizing sanctions, relations with neighboring countries, strengthening public and media diplomacy, documenting war crimes committed by the United States and the Israeli regime, and pursuing the demand for justice and retribution for the martyrs of the Second and Third Imposed Wars. The members of Parliament expressed their appreciation for the efforts and initiatives of the diplomatic apparatus in safeguarding national interests and the rights of the Iranian people, and stressed the need for continued collective efforts to preserve national unity and cohesion, as well as simultaneous support for both the field and diplomacy in defense of Iran’s sovereignty and integrity.

item.title: Baghaei: False-flag operations cannot conceal illegal US-Israeli wars
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei wrote on X that false-flag operations cannot conceal the illegal and criminal nature of the endless wars waged by the United States and the Israeli regime, saying the perpetrators are resorting to lies as they struggle to justify their aggression against Iran. The message is as follows: False flags are an old craft: manufacture the incident, assign the blame, and harvest the consequences. In a world where the American and international public is weary of an unlawful war of aggression against Iran, and where the aggressors have no honest way to justify a war of choice, even a raft made of lies can look like salvation to those who are drowning.

item.title: Iranian MFA Spokesperson writes on X after meeting new German ambassador
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei wrote on X that he had held candid and useful talks with Germany’s new ambassador to Iran, Axel Dittmann, on developments in international relations and shared responsibility for protecting the rule of law and international peace and security. His message reads as follows: Today, I received the new German Ambassador to Iran, Amb Alex Dittmann, and we had an engaging and frank discussion on prevailing trends in international relations. Countering the threats and challenges that jeopardize the rule of law and endanger international peace and security remains a shared responsibility - one that calls for insight, courage, and cooperation.

Ararat Mirzoyan, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Armenia, who is visiting Tehran at the head of a diplomatic delegation, met and held talks with Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, on Monday morning. During the meeting, the two sides discussed and exchanged views on Tehran–Yerevan relations. They reviewed the growing trend of bilateral cooperation in various areas of mutual interest and reaffirmed the determination of the leaders of Iran and Armenia to develop and deepen bilateral relations. The Iranian Foreign Minister, referring to the long-standing and enduring ties between the Iranian and Armenian peoples, emphasized the Islamic Republic of Iran’s approach of seeking to expand relations with its neighbors, particularly in the Caucasus and Central Asia. He stressed that the Islamic Republic attaches special importance to its friendly and steadily growing relations with Armenia and considers the ever-increasing interactions and relations with the countries of the Caucasus and Central Asia as a guarantee of security and peace for all countries of the region and as a means of promoting economic growth and prosperity for the peoples of the region. The Armenian Foreign Minister expressed his pleasure at visiting Tehran, underscored the strategic nature of Iran-Armenia relations and Yerevan’s continued commitment and determination to expand cooperation with Iran, and expressed hope that the two countries’ relations would be further deepened with the signing of the Iran-Armenia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Agreement. During the meeting, the foreign ministers of Iran and Armenia held consultations on ways to further strengthen cooperation in the economic, political, trade, transportation and energy fields. The two sides also discussed and exchanged views on developments in the Caucasus and West and South Asia. The Iranian Foreign Minister, explaining the Islamic Republic of Iran’s positions on the importance of peace and stability in the Caucasus, welcomed the continuation of the positive trend in interactions and relations between the Republic of Armenia and the Republic of Azerbaijan. He announced Iran’s readiness to continue dialogue and multilateral cooperation, including within the 3+3 framework, to help consolidate the peace process and strengthen regional connectivity and cooperation. Araghchi also emphasized the importance of paying attention to the consequences and concerns arising from the presence and interference of third parties in the affairs of the Caucasus region, and said that lasting peace and stability in the region depend on the resolution of regional issues by the countries of the region themselves and preventing interference by extra-regional powers. The Iranian Foreign Minister also briefed his Armenian counterpart on developments in the West Asia region, particularly the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz. Referring to the destructive and dangerous consequences of the US and Israeli regime’s military aggression against Iran, which is the main cause and factor behind insecurity in commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, he stressed: “The Islamic Republic of Iran has firmly defended and will continue to defend its national interests and security, while it has never hesitated to use diplomatic means to prevent the escalation of tensions.” The two sides also discussed and exchanged views on coordination at the level of the United Nations and other multilateral organizations and arrangements.

Sey morning addressed ambassadors, heads of diplomatic missions and representatives of international organizations based in Tehran, outlining the Islamic Republic of Iran’s positions on regional developments and providing a report on the diplomatic activities of the Iranian delegation attendied Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, on Sundayng the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. Referring to the Islamic Republic of Iran’s effective and assertive presence at the UN General Assembly, the Foreign Minister outlined the key activities carried out during his stay in New York, including consultations with the presidents and foreign ministers of more than 60 countries and senior officials of regional and international organizations, as well as talks with think tanks and media outlets. The Foreign Minister, stressing the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to safeguard Iran’s rights and national interests, provided explanations about Iran’s proposed initiative to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, emphasizing that the world has clearly witnessed Iran’s continued goodwill and seriousness in using diplomacy to prevent an escalation of tensions. Araghchi added: “It became clear to everyone at this session that the Islamic Republic of Iran is serious about pursuing diplomacy, just as it is serious and determined in defending itself.” Elaborating on the Islamic Republic of Iran’s principled position regarding US excessive demands, the Foreign Minister stressed that if the adversaries once again choose the path of military confrontation and war, Iran’s response will be much stronger and more decisive than in the past. Araghchi also condemned the disgraceful conduct of US officials toward the delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran, including the claim that members of the delegation had been expelled. He noted that the entry and departure of the Iranian delegation took place according to the previously announced schedule. Nevertheless, US officials, in an attempt to compensate for their failure to portray Iran as isolated, resorted to fabrications and claimed that the Iranian delegation had been expelled. He said this was, on the one hand, an overt admission of the United States’ violation of its international obligations as the host country of the United Nations and, on the other, an indication of US officials’ anger over the Islamic Republic of Iran’s effective presence at the most important international event. Elsewhere in his remarks, the Foreign Minister referred to meetings held with neighboring countries, including the Persian Gulf states, and stressed Iran’s decision to continue the process of building trust among regional countries based on the principle of good-neighborliness, with the aim of strengthening cooperation and coordination to promote regional peace and security. He also referred to meetings with European counterparts and stressed that the Islamic Republic of Iran had conveyed its positions to European foreign ministers on the need for European countries to adopt a responsible and independent approach toward issues concerning West Asia. Referring to repeated acknowledgments by NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte of the direct and extensive participation of European countries in the illegal and aggressive attacks by the United States and Israel against Iran, the Foreign Minister called on European countries to be held accountable for their role in planning and carrying out the US and Israeli regime’s military aggression against Iran. The Foreign Minister, condemning the inhumane and illegal US sanctions against Iran, stressed that sanctions, pressure and threats cannot undermine the Iranian nation’s determination to defend its rights and dignity.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, condemning the illegal and inhumane actions and measures taken by the US government to disrupt Iran’s commercial exchanges and air transportation with other countries through the extraterritorial implementation of illegal US sanctions, stresses that these measures not only run counter to the fundamental principles of the Charter of the United Nations and international law, particularly the principle of respect for the national sovereignty of states, and violate fundamental human rights standards, but also constitute a dangerous plot aimed at undermining friendly relations among countries, particularly neighboring states. In this regard, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, recalling the deep historical, religious, cultural and people-to-people ties between the two nations of Iran and Iraq, and appreciating the fraternal relations and good-neighborly ties between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Republic of Iraq, considers the imposed restrictions on civil air travel between Iran and Iraq to be contrary to the common interests and objectives of the two countries. Relations between Iran and Iraq go beyond the conventional relations between two neighboring countries and are founded on deep people-to-people ties and mutual interests in various fields. The travel of millions of Iranian and Iraqi citizens for economic and commercial activities, pilgrimage to holy sites, tourism, education, and medical treatment necessitates that issues related to transportation and communications between the two nations be managed independently, responsibly and with a forward-looking approach, based on their common interests. The restrictions imposed on air travel between the two countries, in addition to creating serious difficulties for hundreds of thousands of passengers, pilgrims, patients, students and economic actors from the two countries, are in clear contradiction with the nature of the strategic relations and good-neighborly ties between Iran and Iraq. While respecting the national sovereignty of the Republic of Iraq, the Islamic Republic of Iran calls for appropriate decisions to be taken in response to the US economic terrorism and sedition-mongering with a view to lifting the restrictions and restoring normal conditions for flights operated by the airlines of the two countries, in line with the interests and objectives of the two nations.

item.title: Iran urges Canada to answer for fate of indigenous children unmarked graves
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmil Baghaei, in a post on X marking Canada’s National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, called on the Canadian government to provide evidence, transparency and accountability regarding the fate of Indigenous children and unmarked graves linked to the country’s residential school system. That question still haunts the conscience of the world when it comes to the Canada's Indigenous children who were taken from their families, stripped of their names, languages, cultures, and identities, and subjected to a system of forced assimilation. Many suffered abuse and neglect, and many died far from home and buried in unmarked graves. September 30 was Canada’s National Day for Truth and Reconciliation - apparently to honour residential school survivors and their families, and to remember the innocent Indigenous children who never came home. But reconciliation cannot be reduced to a commemorative day or political rhetoric. When serious questions remain unanswered and the history of residential schools is contested or obscured, reconciliation remains incomplete. The suffering of Indigenous children is not a culture war. It is a matter of historical truth and accountability. Questions surrounding unmarked graves deserve evidence, transparency, and an honest examination of the historical record - not denial, distortion, or silence. No reconciliation without truth. No justice without accountability.
